text_blocks.snippet: Basement membrane disease of the eye, specifically Epithelial Basement Membrane Dystrophy (EBMD), is a condition where the cornea's outer layer (epithelium) doesn't properly adhere to the underlying basement membrane. This can lead to various symptoms like fluctuating or blurred vision, and in some cases, painful recurrent corneal erosions.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition where the cornea's outer layer (epithelium) doesn't properly adhere to the underlying basement membrane

list.title: What it is:
list.snippet: EBMD is characterized by an irregular basement membrane in the cornea, causing the epithelium to become loose and prone to detachment.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Common symptoms include blurry or fluctuating vision, especially upon waking, and a gritty or sandy feeling in the eye. Some individuals experience painful corneal erosions, which are small defects in the corneal surface.
